αἰήτης: Aeetes, son of Helius and Perse
αἰθρηγενής: born in ether, sprung from ether
αἱμονίδης: son of Haemon, Maeon, from Thebes
αὐγείας: king in Elis, known from the cleansing of his stables by Heracles
αὐθέντης: one who does by his own hand; a murderer
βοηλάτης: one that drives away oxen, a cattle-lifter
γεννητής: enfranchised member of γένος in Athens
δαρδανίδης: a son or descendant of Dardanos
δεσπότης: a master, lord, the master of the house
δημότης: one of the people, a commoner, plebeian
εἰσηγητής: one who brings in, a mover, author
εὐπατρίδης: of good or noble sire, of noble family
θρανίτης: one of the rowers on the topmost of the three benches
καιάδας: a pit at Sparta, into which criminals were thrown
καταιβάτης: as descending in thunder and lightning
καταποντιστής: one who throws into the sea
κλυτοτέχνης: famous for his art, renowned artist
κορυστής: a helmed man, an armed warrior
κυθηροδίκης: a Spartan magistrate sent annually to govern the island of Cythera
λοχίτης: one of the same company, a fellow-soldier, comrade
λωποδύτης: one who slips into another’s clothes, a clothes-stealer
μετανάστης: one who has changed his home, a wanderer, immigrant
μηλοθύτης: one who sacrifices sheep, a priest
μηριόνης: (pun on pr.n. and μηροί, thighs) female genitals
μικροπολίτης: a citizen of a petty town
μοχλευτής: one who heaves by a lever
ναύτης: a sailor, seaman; a fellow sailor
οἰκιστής: a coloniser, founder of a city
οἰωνιστής: one who foretells from the flight and cries of birds, an augur
παιδοτρίβης: one who teaches boys wrestling and other exercises, a gymnastic master
παρακοίτης: one who sleeps beside, a bedfellow, husband, spouse
παραστάτης: one who stands by, a defender
πατραλοίας: one who slays his father, a parricide
πατριώτης: one of the same country, a fellow-countryman
πελοπίδης: descendant of Pelops, pr. n. Pelopidas
πελταστής: one who bears a light shield
πινακοπώλης: one who sells small birds plucked and ranged upon a board
ποδάρκης: succouring with the feet, running to the rescue
προηγητής: one who goes before to shew the way, a guide
προστάτης: one who stands before, a front-rank-man
προφήτης: one who speaks for a God and interprets his will
πρωταγωνιστής: one who plays the first part, the chief actor
πρωτοστάτης: one who stands first, on the right, the right-hand man
πυλάρτης: gate-fastener, he that keeps the gates of hell
σιτάλκης: Sitalces, king of Odrysians in Thrace; epithet of Apollo at Delphi
στρατηλάτης: a leader of an army, a general, commander
συγκολλητής: one who glues together, a fabricator
σωφρονιστής: one that makes temperate, a chastener, chastiser
τεχνίτης: an artificer, artisan, craftsman, skilled workman
τυνδαρίδης: son of Tyndareus: Castor and Pollux
φιληλιαστής: one who delights in the trials of the court Heliaea
φιλοπότης: a lover of drinking, fond of wine
φυγαίχμης: fleeing from the spear, unwarlike, cowardly
φυλέτης: one of the same tribe, a tribesman
χάρμη: the joy of battle, lust of battle
χαλκοβόας: with voice of brass, i. e. ringing strong and clear
χειροδίκης: one who asserts his right by hand, uses the right of might
ἀγροβότης: feeding in the field, dwelling in the country
ἀθλοθέτης: one who awards the prize, the judge
ἀλείτης: one who flees from punishment, a culprit, a sinner
ἀλφηστής: working for one’s daily bread, laborious, enterprising
ἀπηλιώτης: the wind that comes from the rising sun, the east wind
ἀποστάτης: a runaway slave: a deserter, rebel
ἀριφράδης: easy to be known, very distinct, manifest
ἀσπιστής: one armed with a shield, a warrior
ἀφέτης: one who lets off a military engine
ἀψευδής: without lie and deceit, truthful, sincere, trusty
ἁβροκόμης: with luxuriant foliage; with delicate hair
ἄλτης: king of the Leleges, father of Laothoe
ἐγγυητής: one who gives security, a surety
ἐξηγητής: one who leads on, an adviser
ἑβδομαγέτης: sacrificed on the 7th of every month
ἑρμῆς: Hermes; a statue or bust of Hermes
ἡλικιώτης: an equal in age, fellow, comrade
ἱεροφάντης: a hierophant, one who teaches the rites of sacrifice and worship
ἱκέτης: one who comes to seek protection, a suppliant
ἱππηλάτης: a driver of horses, one who fights from a chariot, a Knight
ἱππιοχάρμης: one who fights from a chariot
ὀλυμπιονίκης: a conqueror in the Olympic games
ὀπίας: cheese from milk curdled with fig-juice
ὀρέστης: Orestes; pl., the Orestae, an Epirot people
ὀρφανιστής: a tender of orphans, a guardian
ὑβριστής: a violent, overbearing person, a wanton, insolent man
ὑληκοίτης: one who lodges in the wood
ὑπηνήτης: one that is just getting a beard, with one’s first beard
ὑποστάτης: that which stands under, a support, prop
ὑποφήτης: a suggester, interpreter, a priest who declares an oracle
ὑφηγητής: one who leads the way, a guide, leader
